title: Design brief & creative brief

body.text: A good brief is half the design work done — have the AI help
turn the client's vague wants into a clear brief
: goals, target audience, scope, deliverables, and success criteria.

example: "The client just said 'I want a logo that looks expensive' — help me come up with 10 questions to ask so I can write a brief that actually works"

title: A brief structure that works

body.text: problem/opportunity · target users · key message · deliverables · timeline · what NOT to do
— the last one matters a lot, e.g. don't use the competitor's colors, no cartoon fonts for a finance brand.

example: "From these client meeting notes, draft a design brief following the 6-point structure; where there isn't enough info, mark what I still need to ask"

question: What does the AI help with when a client's wants are vague?

options.text: Asks questions that turn the vagueness into a clear brief
Guesses what the client means and just does it

question: Which is a component of a good brief?

options.text: Target users, key message, and what NOT to do

question: Why is 'what NOT to do' important in a brief?

options.text: It keeps the work within the brand's bounds from the start, saving rework

question: To get a workable creative brief, what should you specify?

options.text: Goals, target audience, scope, and tone

question: What does a good design brief help with?

options.text: It gets the team on the same page before starting
It just slows the work down
